editorial.brief: Patrick Stewart, reported dead at 86 on Lemmy, drew 2,356,552 Wikipedia views, six times the next article, and the story also appears on Hacker News and Mastodon. Elsewhere, Hacker News weighed Mistral Large 4 weights at 1,288 points and a claimed $5.6B Binance theft at 989. A M6.4 quake struck near Easter Island.
editorial.cover_sub: Patrick Stewart took 2,356,552 Wikipedia views on a day when Lemmy ran three posts reporting his death and Mastodon filled with farewells; the runner-up, .xxx, managed 390,246.
editorial.wiki_deck: Reports of Patrick Stewart's death at 86 sent 2,356,552 readers to his Wikipedia page, six times the audience of the runner-up. Lemmy and Mastodon were saying the same thing.
editorial.letter_headline: One obituary, six times the next story
editorial.discourse_deck: Hacker News is busy with open model weights and a claimed $5.6B Binance theft, Lemmy is in mourning with a House report alongside, Bluesky is posting ketchup packets, and Mastodon mourns and frets over Proton.
editorial.foreign_deck: The wire is all AI: over $100 million for US STEM, a pricing suit against McDonald, and Indian graduates short of entry-level jobs. Searchers asked about Alphabet's stock drop.
editorial.markets_deck: All five markets are political: three on the US midterms, two on Israel. The largest, $3M, prices Republican House control at 7%, and Likud's seat market is at 99%.
editorial.watch_deck: Counter-Strike 2 peaked at 1,207,353 players on Steam, ahead of PUBG at 785,066, Phantom Blade Zero at 723,876 and Dota 2 at 708,985. On Twitch, caseoh_ holds 62,237 viewers, TheBurntPeanut 36,464.
editorial.yt_note: Jisoo leads at 2,186,994 views, followed by a Worlds Swiss Stage match at 1,686,224. The Apex Legends Cipher trailer, at 470,329 views, also appears on Steam's list.
editorial.closing_note: By tomorrow's edition the Stewart obituary will have cooled in the Wikipedia count, and the ketchup packets, the Easter Island M6.4 and the Mistral weights will be older news. Only the Cloudflare domains, google.com first, are likely to look the same.
wiki_paras: Patrick Stewart topped Wikipedia's most-read list with 2,356,552 views. Lemmy supplies the reason: its top post, at 1,302 points, reports that he died at 86, and two more posts with 703 and 692 points say the same. Headlines name him as Captain Picard of Star Trek and Charles Xavier of X-Men.

The margin is wide. Second place, the .xxx domain, drew 390,246 views, and third, the 2026 Israeli legislative election, drew 363,543. Stewart's total is six times the runner-up. Sunny Ozell, fourth at 346,682, and William Contreras, fifth at 228,487, were left a long way behind.

Mastodon posts mourn a voice and a legend, and one writer says they rarely post about celebrity deaths. The cluster tags Hacker News as well, though none of its five leading titles names him. It is the day's only story on three feeds, and the Wikipedia count suggests readers went looking for the record of a long career.
letter_paras: Today is a single-story day. Patrick Stewart leads Wikipedia and Lemmy, Mastodon follows, and the margin over second place on Wikipedia is 6.0x. The rest of the snapshot is scattered: model weights, a claimed Binance theft, an Israeli election, an M6.4 quake near Easter Island. None of them came near the obituary for attention.

The unglamorous corners were busy in their own way. USGS logged 25 quakes of M2.5 or above in 24 hours. Bluesky's contribution was advice to hand out the year's accumulated ketchup packs at Halloween. Cloudflare's top domains were google.com, googleapis.com, amazonaws.com, cloudflare.com and gstatic.com, which is to say the plumbing.

A same-hour snapshot removes the lag that a roundup introduces. Every feed is read at one moment, so a name appearing in three places is attention arriving together, not a rumour passed along. A weekly summary would flatten today into a sentence. One hour's reading keeps the proportions, including the 6.0x gap, intact.

brief: Patrick Stewart, reported dead at 86 on Lemmy, drew 2,356,552 Wikipedia views, six times the next article, and the story also appears on Hacker News and Mastodon.
